newsitem.title: USA: Gore silent on Supreme Court's Paula Jones ruling.
newsitem.headline: Gore silent on Supreme Court's Paula Jones ruling.

text.p: U.S. Vice President Al Gore on Tuesday referred all questions about the Supreme Court ruling on the Paula Jones sexual harassment suit to President Bill Clinton's lawyers.
"I have no reaction or comment and I would urge that you direct any questions to his personal lawyers and they'll respond to that," Gore told reporters during a campaign stop in New Hampshire.
Asked if he would be the Democratic candidate for president in 2000, Gore said there were still 987 days to go before the New Hampshire primary, the first presidential primary.
Earlier Tuesday, a unanimous Supreme Court ruled that Jones's sexual harassment lawsuit against Clinton could proceed immediately rather than wait until he leaves office.

The court rejected Clinton's arguments that allowing the lawsuit to go forward while he remained in the White House would prove a significant distraction, hindering the performance of his presidential duties.

The ruling involved only when the case could go forward, not the merits of Jones' allegations that Clinton made unwanted advances in 1991 in a Little Rock hotel room when he was governor of Arkansas and she was a state employee.
